title: fix(sse): correct chunking/framing ordering and delimiter handling for partial JSON streaming
author: Ava Chen
description: Background: clients using the OpenAI-compatible SSE streaming layer sometimes receive malformed/partial JSON when message boundaries and token emission ordering cause structural characters (e.g. '}', ']', commas) to be emitted in a different event than their object contents. This leads to client-side JSON parsing errors and broken function/tool-calling flows. This PR fixes chunking and framing behavior in the SSE emitter and chunker so that partial JSON fragments are ordered and delimited deterministically, avoids emitting closing delimiters in isolation, and preserves logical token/event ordering for function/tool-calling and structured output. Changes include: 1) chunker: make delimiter tokens (commas, braces, brackets) sticky to the previous event when they complete a JSON token boundary; 2) sse_emitter: ensure event timestamps and sequence numbers are monotonic and used to order events before sending; 3) openai_compat adapter: update streaming adapter to reassemble partial JSON with a small lookback window to avoid transient parse errors for clients that expect complete JSON per event; 4) tests: add unit and integration tests that fuzz-simulate token splits and verify parsing for streaming structured responses and tool/function calls; 5) docs: document known compatibility considerations and recommended backoff for client parsers. Motivation: improve streaming stability for structured outputs (partial JSON), function/tool calling, and OpenAI compatibility, prioritizing minimal latency impact while reducing parse failures in downstream clients. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced failure with fuzz tests - [x] Implemented chunker and emitter fixes - [x] Added regression tests for function calling streams - [x] Updated OpenAI compatibility adapter - [x] Benchmarked latency/regression impact (~+0.2ms median per-event) - [x] Updated docs and release notes

release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming chunking and framing — prevents partial JSON delimiter splits that caused client-side parse errors.
Improvement: OpenAI compatibility adapter now reassembles partial JSON with a small lookback to avoid transient failures during function/tool calling streams.
Notes: This is a backwards-compatible change; clients may observe a small per-event latency increase (~0.2ms median) but significantly fewer parse errors for structured streaming output.
